This position resides within the Primary Care Service Line at the Dakota Dunes Community Based Outpatient Clinic (CBOC) within the Sioux Falls VA Healthcare System. Reviews consults, completes patient history, examination, diagnosis, treatment and education for new and follow up patient visits.

Documents in SOAP (Subjective, Objective, Assessment, Plan) format, respond to Clinical Reminders, and order appropriate lab tests and studies by Provider Order Entry. Responsible for interpreting as appropriate and the implementation of results & recommendations from studies ordered.

Initiates and adjusts medications as medically necessary, practices & maintains skills in EKG, and recommends appropriate follow up. Completes electronic encounter for each visit and conducts telephone clinics and responds to patient phone calls as appropriate.

Respects time commitments, provides customer service appropriate to VA standards, and provides patient care through face to face visits and other modalities (group clinics, telephone clinics, secure messaging, etc.).

Performs oversight of primary care clinical studies to include appropriate scheduling of patients, patient flow, safety, quality management, capacity, backlogs, results reporting, wait times, and consults.

Utilizes PACT and ACA principles, assists in meeting Performance Measures for Primary Care outpatient clinics, and coordinates care for patients as appropriate between specialty medicine, mental health, surgical/surgical sub-specialty, extended care and rehabilitation, community, and other ancillary services.

Maintains awareness of costs incurred for fee basis, contracting, and VA care. Balances costs and productivity with quality patient care and customer service. Participates in Peer Review and works as a team with medical doctor, nursing, technicians, administration, lab, pharmacy, dieticians, and ancillary staff.

Completes CME, TMS, HIPAA, Security training, and other training as mandated by VA. Serves on committees, teams, workgroups, and chart reviews as requested/approved by administration.

Advanced Practice Nurse (Nurse Practitioner) Basic Requirements Education: A post-master's certificate or master's or doctoral degree as a Nurse Practitioner.

(Applicants pending the completion of educational requirements may be referred and tentatively selected but may not be hired until the education requirements are met.) Must be a graduate of a school of professional nursing approved by the appropriate accrediting agency and accredited by one of the following accrediting bodies at the time the program was completed by the applicant: The Accreditation Commission for Education in Nursing (ACEN) or The Commission on Collegiate Nursing Education (CCNE).

NOTE: Foreign Education. Graduates of foreign schools of professional nursing programs, the nurse practitioner degree equivalency must be validated through an Agency recognized degree equivalency evaluation agency, such as the International Consultants of Delaware (ICD).

Candidates with equivalent nurse practitioner masters or doctorate level degrees who possess current, full, active, and unrestricted registration and certification will meet the requirement of graduation from an approved school of professional nursing to warrant appointment.

License - All APN (NPs) must possess and maintain an active, current, full, and unrestricted APN license to practice as an NP in a State, Territory or Commonwealth of the United States, or in the District of Columbia.

Basic Board Certification - All APN (NPs) must maintain full and current basic board certification in one of the following: Family Nurse Practitioner (FNP), Adult Nurse Practitioner (ANP), Adult-Gerontology Primary Care Nurse Practitioner (AGPCNP), or Gerontology Nurse Practitioner (GNP) from one of the following: the American Nurses Credentialing Center (ANCC), American Academy of Nurse Practitioners Certification Board (AANPCB), or other nationally recognized certifying body in the area in which the Nurse Practitioner is academically prepared.

NOTE: Grandfathering Provision - All persons currently employed in VHA in 0610 series and an APN (NP) assignment that are also performing the duties as described in the qualification standard on the effective date of the standard (1/29/2024) are considered to have met all qualification requirements for the grade held including positive education and licensure/certification.

The following Scope, Education and Experience, and Dimension criteria must be met to qualify for Advanced Practice Nurse (Nurse Practitioner) II: Exception to Licensure for Graduate Nurse Technicians.

Candidates who otherwise meet the basic requirements, but do not possess the required licensure and/or certification, may be appointed at the entry step of the Nurse II, as a Graduate Nurse Technician - Nurse Practitioner on a temporary appointment up to any period not-to-exceed one year and a day under the authority of 38 U.S.C. § 405(c)(2)(B).

Scope: Demonstrates leadership in delivering and improving holistic care through collaborative strategies with others Education and Experience Requirement: Meets basic education requirement for APN (NP). Nurse II is considered the entry grade level for APN (NPs); no experience is required.

Dimension Requirement: APNs (NPs) at level II are expected to meet the following dimension requirements: Clinical Practice. Delivers evidence-based health care, demonstrating proficiency in the ability to manage a patient panel, population, or program. Outcome Focus.

Utilizes research and evidence-based practice to evaluate the patient care delivery system within a patient panel or program, presents findings and contributes to changes that enhance the quality and timeliness of veteran/patient care. Leadership.

Works effectively as a leader within a team/unit/group and seeks interdisciplinary collaboration as appropriate to enhance patient care. Professional Development. Acquires knowledge and skills to develop expertise in area of practice. Professionalism/Collegiality.

Demonstrates effective communication skills and professional behavior, promoting cooperation and teamwork. Participates in interdisciplinary teams and processes that positively impact patient outcomes.

The following Scope, Education and Experience, and Dimension criteria must be met to qualify for Advanced Practice Nurse (Nurse Practitioner) III: Scope: Executes position responsibilities that demonstrate leadership, experience, and creative approaches to management of complex client care.

Education and Experience Requirement: Meets basic education requirement for an APN (NP) AND one year of specialized APN (NP) experience equivalent to the Nurse II grade level. Dimension Requirement: APN (Nurse Practitioners) at grade III are expected to meet the following dimension requirements: Clinical Practice.

Influences and models the delivery of evidence- based health care, demonstrating expertise in the ability to manage a patient panel, population, or program. Outcome Focus. Leads and implements changes that enhance the quality and timeliness of Veteran/patient care applying research and evidence in the delivery of healthcare for patient populations.

Leadership. Initiates and leads interdisciplinary teams informed by structured approaches and processes to improve outcomes that positively impact care for a patient panel, population, or program. Professional Development. Acquires knowledge and skills, then disseminates acquired information within and/or outside the medical facility.

Professionalism/Collegiality. Initiates and leads interdisciplinary teams developing systems that positively impact outcomes at the panel, population, or program level. Demonstrates effective communication skills and professional behavior, promoting cooperation and teamwork.

The Assistant Nurse Manager, Patient Flow is responsible for facilitating the fulfillment of the VA Northern California Health Care System's mission, vision, values, and strategic direction within the Patient Flow department and as a member of the NCHCS leadership team.

The incumbent is an important facilitator of interdisciplinary effectiveness and communication that reaches outside of the department towards applicable community resources and relevant program offices within the Veterans Health Administration.

The incumber is member of the team caring for a diverse group of Veterans in various stages of the life cycle. The incumbent executes position responsibilities that demonstrate leadership, experience, and creative approaches to management of complex patient care.

The incumbent is responsible for the documented outcomes at the program or service level. Major duties include, but are not limited to the following: Provide leadership and service excellence in patient throughput with oversight of the day to day operations of the Patient Flow Department.

Leadership responsibilities also include personnel management for Utilization Management, patient placement staff, Nurse Supervisors and patient support services, (i.e., intermittent and float pool staff).

Direct the system-wide Bed Management System (BMS) and Emergency Department Integration System (EDIS) including integration with other support departments. You will provide appropriate reports to monitor patient throughput initiatives within the organization.

Collaborates with all disciplines to ensure that the discharge/transfer of patients is achieved in a way that meets the needs of the patient and complies with priorities for action targets.

Collaborates with clinical teams in ensuring that all patients requiring admission are placed in the most appropriate clinical environment available within the four-hour standard. Demonstrates competence in current knowledge of specific unit placement criteria (i.e., BMS, EDIS).

Analyzes performance of patient throughput systems and protocols using critical thinking skills. Demonstrates and communicates commitment to performance improvement through unit-based teams and a culture of engagement.

Standardize communications and expectations across disciplines Establish and enforce standard work for nursing care that is consistent, clear, and available to staff. Utilizes patient flow technology to help teams focus on common goals. Ensures that appropriate resources and processes are in place to manage and maintain new technologies.

Responsible for direct coordination of staffing, physical facilities, supplies and equipment for nursing services to patients on a 24 hour, 7 day a week basis.

Manages the delivery of quality patient care, including accurate and appropriate documentation, employees clinical/performance competency and continuous National and VANCHCS Performance Improvement Measures, consistent with VANCHCS mission. Accountable for successfully building and reinforcing essential programs.

Serves as a change agent and actively participates in systematically evaluating existing programs, planning new programs, and implementing changes in clinical standards of care. Implements action plans to effect positive change.

Oversees and monitors employee's adherence to VHA Privacy/HIPPA and Information Security Responsible for retention and recruitment of highly skilled nursing staff, monitoring changes in work flow, technical and equipment needs, and ensuring a workforce that can adapt to a rapidly changing environment.

Provides oversight to ensure that standards of practice are met within the department. Assures nursing competencies are developed and implemented to ensure competence in providing care. Responsible for ensuring employees complete mandatory annual and on time facility and nursing training and reviews within mandated time frame.

Responsible for ensuring annual appraisals/proficiencies are completed, communicated to the employees and submitted in a timely manner. Manages and reinforces VANCHCS time and leave policies. Ensures time management procedures are followed accurately.

Assists manager in approval of personnel timecards, leave requests, and monitor leave usage VA offers a comprehensive total rewards package: VA Nurse Total Rewards Pay: Competitive salary, regular salary increases, potential for performance awards Paid Time Off: 50 days of paid time off per year (26 days of annual leave, 13 days of sick leave, 11 paid Federal holidays per year) Retirement: Traditional federal pension (5 years vesting) and federal 401K with up to 5% in contributions by VA Insurance: Federal health/vision/dental/term life/long-term care (many federal insurance programs can be carried into retirement) Licensure: 1 full and unrestricted license from any US State or territory Work Schedule: M - F 7:30- 4:00 Telework: No available Virtual: This is NOT a virtual position.

Physical Requirements: This clinical position includes a level of physicality normally associated with direct patient care duties performed by nurses such as potentially long periods of continued walking, standing, sitting, moderate lifting, repeated bending, or kneeling.

Preferred Experience: Minimum of 3-5 years of Supervisory experience, knowledge of hospital operations and interdepartmental workflow.

Major duties: Assumes responsibility for the coordination of care focused on patient education, self-management, and customer satisfaction throughout the continuum of care. Administers procedures per established policies and guidelines. Influences care outcomes by collaborating with members of the interdisciplinary team.

May participate in the systematic evaluation of current practice, development, coordination, and management of the patient care programs. Serves as a consultant for problem resolution.

Maintains flexibility with a high degree of interpersonal skills, effective communication, leadership, motivation, self-direction, and ongoing evaluation of activities.

Utilizes the nursing process in assessment, planning, implementation, and evaluation of quality and safe care of Veterans evidenced by comprehensive management of patient safety standards and best practices.

Core elements of performance include knowledge and active participation in the unit/program level quality improvement process and initiatives as well as customer service programs.

The Registered Nurse (RN) is responsible for providing competent, evidence-based care to a patient population with oversight of licensed vocational nurses/nursing assistants as appropriate to the setting.

The nurse will assist in directing the provision of nursing education, orientation, competencies and providing quality improvement and outcomes utilization. This nurse integrates knowledge, skills, abilities, and judgment and is self-directed in goal setting for managing complex situations.

Demonstrates proficiency in decision-making and using the nursing process for complex situations that effect performance outcomes at the point of care. Practice is enhanced through development of collegial relationships. Demonstrates leadership and collaboration by using the group process to solve problems.

The focus is on leadership in strategically planning long-term goals for the microsystem (unit, team, or workgroup) that impacts operations or resources. Demonstrates the ability to cope with and manage competing priorities.

The nurse demonstrates competence in practice and decision-making, deliberate planning, integrating theoretical concepts, critical thinking skills, and technically skilled practice. Acts as a role model, mentor, and coach to the program's staff. Is a key member of the interdisciplinary team to promote effective and safe care.

An addendum is available for specific position duties.

The Registered Nurse may be exposed to infected patients and contaminated materials and may be required to don protective clothing in isolation situations or operative/invasive procedures.

The RN - Wound Care is a professional nurse (RN) with extensive clinical and technical knowledge in wound care. This person is responsible to assess, plan, evaluate, coordinate and establish the individualized care plan for all residents/patients with wound/ostomy needs.

The wound care RN is certified and their scope includes inpatient areas, outpatient areas and the CLC. Provide and assess variety of wounds, including pressure ulcers, and arterial, venous, diabetic, traumatic, burns and skin tears. Complete wound assessment including picture taking and downloading to CPRS.

Educate nursing staff about pressure ulcer staging, wound descriptions and partial and full thickness wounds. Educate nursing staff, veterans and significant others about wound and ostomy care. Complete negative pressure wound therapy and complete dressing changes. Provide care and education in acute care, ICU, CLC and outpatient clinic setting.

Participate in new employee orientation and educate visiting nursing and dietary students. Provide ostomy care and education pre and post-operative. This includes stoma measuring, assisting with the correct pouching system.

Educating veteran and care givers in regards to stoma care and applying wafer/ pouch, as well as troubleshooting a stomal/peri-stomal complications that may arise. Collaborate with surgery and primary care physicians to provide and plan of care. Collaborate with physicians to provide continuity of care.

Collaborate with Community Health Nursing staff and Home Health agencies to provide the best care for our Veterans out in the community. Manage Wound care RN outpatient wound care clinic, scheduling, recommend treatments, and work with other disciplines including Primary care physicians, surgery staff, and community health nurse.

The Charge Nurse duties will focus on day-to-day clinical operations. They emphasize immediate patient care, oversight of staff during that period, and operational stability during busy or unpredictable moments.

The role of a Charge Nurse "aims to enhance nurse retention, bolster teamwork, improve patient safety, and raise overall quality of care." They function as a role model, educator, while providing guidance to the team.

Duties include but are not limited to: In collaboration with the Nurse Manager, functions as an operational lead and assumes accountability for the operation of all areas within the role Serve as the operational lead for the nursing team to ensure that clinics run smoothly and that patient care needs are met in a coordinated, timely manner Lead staff by coordinating care, supporting staff, and responding quickly when unexpected challenges arise Contributing to the establishment and implementation of evidence-based nursing standards of practice.

Accountable for adhering to established policies, standards of care and standards of practice, demonstrating leadership in improving nursing care, as well as other duties as assigned. Providing direct patient care by assessing patient needs and making clinical decisions by monitoring patient conditions and responding to changes.

Coordinating treatment plans and ensuring correct execution while collaborating with physicians and other members of care teams to refine care strategies.

Administering medications and performing procedures as needed Assigning clinic duties to nursing staff based on acuity and staff skill levels Providing guidance and mentorship to newer or less experienced staff Acting as a liaison between the nursing team and other departments Stepping in to resolve conflicts or clarify orders when delays occur Informing Veterans and their families about unit procedures or status changes Reporting staffing changes or concerns, managing supplies and ensuring necessary equipment is available, responding to documentation needs, including chart audits to ensure accuracy while ensuring compliance with evidenced based practice for infection control and safety standards Reporting incidents or quality concerns to leadership and follow through with steps to resolve and ensure safe quality care.

Champions Peer to Peer Chart Audit process Inspecting clinics for environmental safety and cleanliness compliance, maintains list of work orders from entry to resolution.

Serves a vital, behind-the-scenes role to ensure smooth coordination and case flow between the Operating Room (OR), the Sterile Processing Department (SPD), and logistics.

Follows procedures per established policies and guidelines, influences care outcomes by collaborating with members of the interdisciplinary team, and executes position responsibilities that demonstrate leadership, experience, and creative approaches to management of complex client care.

The duties include but are not limited to: The Perioperative Program Coordinator is a registered nurse who provides leadership and coordination across the OR, Sterile Processing, Logistics, Prosthetics, Engineering, and other departments to ensure smooth surgical operations.

The role oversees procurement and management of surgical supplies, equipment, and instrumentation; develops and updates protocols for new products; manages vendor interactions and loaner items; and ensures stock levels, implants, and case carts are accurate and properly maintained. .

The Coordinator works closely with the OR Scheduler, Implant Coordinator, and Medical Instrument Technicians (MITs), and is cross trained to support scheduling and implant coordination functions as needed. .

The Coordinator collaborates with SPS and Logistics staff to process supply requests, maintain appropriate par levels on supply carts, and evaluate instrumentation sets to meet service needs, providing written updates for any changes. The Coordinator has case cart knowledge and works with OR staff to ensure case carts are accurate.

The Coordinator facilitates communication between departments, aligns workflows, and troubleshoots issues related to surgical supplies, instrumentation, equipment availability, and case preparation.

Coordinator plays a key role in preventing delays, promoting interdisciplinary collaboration, and maintaining consistent readiness of surgical suites through proactive planning and problem-solving.

Arbeitsort: Hirslanden Klinik Hirslanden \| Zürich
Besetzung per: 01. Dezember 2026 oder nach Vereinbarung
Anstellungsart: Unbefristet
Referenznummer: 72993
Als grösstes medizinisches Netzwerk der Schweiz setzen wir mit unseren Kliniken, ambulanten Operationszentren und Notfallstationen
Du suchst eine Aufgabe, bei der du deine Führungskompetenz einbringen und gleichzeitig nah am Patienten arbeiten kannst?
Auf unserer Privatstation erwartet dich ein professionelles Umfeld, in dem du gemeinsam mit deinem Team für eine erstklassige Betreuung unserer Patientinnen und Patienten sorgst.

* Unterstützung der Leitung Bettenabteilung im personellen und administrativen Bereich
* Mitarbeit in der Pflege ca. 80%
* Sicherstellung einer professionellen sowie qualitativ erstklassigen Betreuung der Patienten unter Berücksichtigung unseres Pflegeleitbildes
* Unterstützung in der Einführung und Betreuung von neuen Mitarbeitenden, Lernenden sowie Studierenden

* Abgeschlossene Ausbildung zur/zum Pflegefachfrau/-mann sowie entsprechende Führungsweiterbildung oder die Bereitschaft, diese zu absolvieren
* SRK-Anerkennung bei ausländischen Diplomen

* Mindestens drei Jahre Berufserfahrung im Akutbereich
* Bereits erste Führungserfahrung ab Stufe Stv. Leitung Bettenabteilung in einem Schweizer Akutspital
* Sehr gute Deutschkenntnisse (mündlich / schriftlich)
* Gepflegte Umgangsformen und ausgeprägte Serviceorientierung sowie Freude in einem professionellen Umfeld zu arbeiten
Nebst einem attraktiven Arbeitsplatz auf der rechten Seite des Zürichsees erwartet dich ein inter- und multiprofessionell arbeitendes eingespieltes Team. Du arbeitest mit einem zeitgemässen Medizinischen Klinik-Informationssystem und kannst umfangreiche Weiterbildungs- sowie Entwicklungsmöglichkeiten von uns erwarten.

Für die optimale Work-Life-Balance bieten wir flexible Arbeitsbedingungen, die es Müttern und Vätern gleichermaßen erlauben, Berufstätigkeit und Familienaufgaben miteinander zu verbinden. Wir entlohnen regional marktgerecht und bieten attraktive Sozial- sowie Lohnnebenleistungen.

Mitarbeitende, die sich für ihre Arbeit vollständig umziehen müssen, erhalten bei einem 100% Arbeitspensum vier zusätzliche, bezahlte freie Tage. Bei einem reduzierten Arbeitspensum vermindern sich die freien Tage entsprechend. Im Stundenlohn angestellte Mitarbeitende profitieren von einer gleichwertigen finanziellen Abgeltung.

Diese und zahlreiche mehr sind Gründe, weshalb die Klinik Hirslanden zu den attraktivsten Arbeitgebern im Schweizer Gesundheitswesen gehört.
[**Unsere Benefits \| Klinik Hirslanden**](https://www.hirslanden.ch/de/klinik-hirslanden/jobs-und-karriere/hirslanden-als-arbeitgeberin.html)
Für zusätzliche Informationen steht dir Alexandra Filipa Matos Rodrigues, Leiter/in Bettenabteilung, unter filipa.matosrodrigues@hirslanden.ch oder Janine Céline Moschetto unter janine.moschetto@hirslanden.ch gerne zur Verfügung. Wir freuen uns auf deine Kontaktaufnahme.
Bitte beachte, dass wir weder Papierdossiers (werden nicht retourniert) noch Bewerbungen per E-Mail berücksichtigen können. Bitte bewirb dich daher ausschliesslich online über dieses Tool.
Gemischte Teams arbeiten besser. Wir sind stolz auf die Erfahrungen von über 10'000 Mitarbeitenden aus mehr als 80 Nationen. Ihr Wissen und ihre Erfahrungen sind unsere Stärke. Tagtäglich fördern wir Diversität, Chancengleichheit und gleiche Bezahlung für gleiche Arbeit. So wurden wir auch von der Financial Times im Jahr 2021 als einer der \ der Gesundheitsbranche in Europa ausgezeichnet.
**Die Hirslanden-Gruppe** ist das grösste medizinische Netzwerk der Schweiz. Die Gruppe umfasst 16 Kliniken in 9 Kantonen. Sie betreibt zudem 5 ambulante Operationszentren, 18 Radiologie- und 6 Radiotherapieinstitute. Die Gruppe zählt 11 025 Mitarbeitende.

# Fallführende Pflegefachperson HF/FH 80-100% - Raus aus dem Schichtkarussell. Rein in die Fallführung... #
**Ihre Aufgabe:**
Sie begleiten Menschen, die zu Hause gepflegt werden, sowie deren Angehörige. Dabei sind Sie nicht einfach ausführende Pflegefachperson, sondern fachliche Ansprechperson, Berater und Koordinator.
**Sie**
* klären Pflegesituationen und den individuellen Bedarf ab
* erstellen und überprüfen Pflegeplanungen
* beraten, instruieren und begleiten Angehörige
* stellen die fachliche Qualität der Pflege sicher
* dokumentieren sauber und zeitnah
* koordinieren bei Bedarf mit Ärzten und weiteren involvierten Stellen
* übernehmen einen wesentlichen administrativen Anteil
* leisten punktuell praktische Pflege- und Pikettdienste

* Sie verfügen über ein in der Schweiz anerkanntes Pflegediplom HF/FH/DNII/AKP und bringen mehrere Jahre Berufserfahrung mit
* Idealerweise kennen Sie die ambulante Pflege bereits aus eigener Erfahrung. **Spitex-Praxis ist deshalb ein grosses Plus**

* selbstständige und strukturierte Arbeitsweise
* gute kommunikative Fähigkeiten
* Freude an Beratung und Begleitung
* Sicherheit in Administration und Dokumentation
* organisatorisches Geschick und gesunder Pragmatismus
* Führerausweis Kategorie B
* gute IT-Anwenderkenntnisse
